encoding and text: JSON and Regular Expressions

This page lists the extern functions in sa_std/encoding/json.sai and sa_std/text/regex.sai. After reading it, you will be able to parse JSON and fetch values by key, generate JSON with a writer, and compile and match regular expressions.

encoding/json.sai

JSON documents and child nodes are opaque owned ptrs that must be freed with sa_json_free; stringification results are owned buffer handles.

SignatureDescription
sa_json_parse(&json_bytes: ptr, len: u64) -> ^ptrParse JSON text into a root node
sa_json_kind(node: ptr) -> u32Node kind (object/array/string/number, etc.)
sa_json_object_get(node: ptr, &key: ptr, key_len: u64, &out_handle: ptr) -> i32Get a child node by key; sa_json_array_get(node, index, ...) gets one by index
sa_json_object_get_string / _get_bool / _get_i64 / _get_f64(node, &key, key_len, &out_...) -> i32Get a scalar directly by key
sa_json_as_i64 / _as_f64 / _as_bool(node: ptr, &out_value: ptr) -> i32Convert the current node to a scalar
sa_json_string_ptr(node: ptr) -> &ptr / sa_json_string_len(node: ptr) -> u64A string node's data and length
sa_json_value_count(node: ptr, &out_count: ptr) -> i32Number of members/elements; sa_json_object_key_at gets the nth key
sa_json_stringify(node: ptr, &out_handle: ptr) -> i32Serialize into a JSON text buffer
sa_json_buffer_data(buffer: ptr) -> &ptr / _len(buffer) -> u64 / _free(^buffer) -> i32!The buffer trio
sa_json_free(^node: ptr) -> i32!Release a node tree

Streaming Scanning and the Writer

SignatureDescription
sa_json_scanner_new(&out_handle: ptr) -> i32 + _feed / _end_input / _next / _freeA token scanner fed bytes incrementally
sa_json_stream_new(&json_bytes: ptr, len: u64) -> ^ptr + _next / _get_slice_ptr / _get_slice_len / _freeStreaming traversal over existing text
sa_json_writer_new(whitespace: u32, emit_null_optional_fields: u8, emit_strings_as_arrays: u8, escape_unicode: u8, emit_nonportable_numbers_as_strings: u8, &out_handle: ptr) -> i32Create a writer; five options control the output style
sa_json_writer_begin_object / end_object / begin_array / end_array(writer: ptr) -> i32Structure control
sa_json_writer_field_i64(writer: ptr, &key: ptr, key_len: u64, value: i64) -> i32Write an object field; similar functions exist for string/bool/f64/null/node, and key-less write_* variants
sa_json_writer_finish(writer: ptr, &out_handle: ptr) -> i32 or sa_json_writer_finish_buffer(writer: ptr) -> ptrFinish and obtain the output

Numeric Model: Three States (TS-26, Written 2026-10-29)

The numeric representation of a JSON node is three-state, not a single f64 type: .integer (i64), .float (f64), .number_string (raw text). Parsing rules: a literal in integer form that falls within i64 → .integer, exact; an integer exceeding i64 → .number_string, preserved as the original text; a non-integer that is finite → .float; a non-finite value → .number_string. Accessor rules: sa_json_as_i64 is exact for .integer, for .float requires an integral value within the i64 range, and for .number_string performs integer parsing, with overflow being InvalidArgument; sa_json_as_f64 rounds large integers as floating point (integers above 2^53 lose precision via the f64 path, and must go through the i64 / original-text path). stringify writes a .number_string back verbatim, so parse → write-back is lossless for arbitrarily large integers.

text/regex.sai

SignatureDescription
sa_regex_compile(&pattern: ptr, pattern_len: u64, cflags: i32) -> ^ptrCompile a regular expression; flags have POSIX cflags semantics
sa_regex_match(regex: ptr, &text: ptr, text_len: u64) -> ^ptrExecute a match, returning a match object
sa_regex_group_count(regex: ptr) -> u64Number of capture groups
sa_regex_group_ptr(match: ptr, group_idx: u32) -> &ptr / sa_regex_group_len(match: ptr, group_idx: u32) -> u64Read the text range of a capture group
sa_regex_match_free(^match: ptr) -> i32! / sa_regex_free(^regex: ptr) -> i32!Release the match first, then the regex

A Real Example

Sla calling JSON macros directly, from sa_plugin_sla/tests/test_unit_imported_json_direct.sla:

@import "sa_std/string.sa"
@import "sa_std/encoding/json.sa"
@import "import_fixtures/pkgjson/json_helpers.sa"

fn imported_json_kind(data: ptr, data_len: int) -> int {
    let root = JSON_PARSE(data, data_len);
    return JSON_KIND(root);
}

fn imported_json_get_type(data: ptr, data_len: int) -> int {
    let root = JSON_PARSE(data, data_len);
    let t = SLA_JSON_OBJECT_GET(root, STR_PTR("types"), STR_LEN("types"));
    return JSON_KIND(t);
}

Here SLA_JSON_OBJECT_GET is a project-side wrapper macro that expands to an @sa_json_object_get(...) call (see tests/import_fixtures/pkgjson/json_helpers.sa).

NoteIn the tests, a root node's kind is 7 and a string node's kind is 5 — for the specific enumeration values of sa_json_kind, please use the runtime header file as authoritative; do not guess from memory.
